distinguishing_note: A positive dechallenge followed by a positive rechallenge in the same distribution, with no concomitant drugs and no significant comorbidity, leaves no competing explanation with meaningful support.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Drug C caused the maculopapular rash
hypotheses.label_rationale: Exposure preceded the rash, withdrawal resolved it, and an inadvertent re-exposure reproduced it within twelve hours in the same distribution. No concomitant drugs and no significant comorbidity were present to explain it otherwise.

supporting_evidence.statement: Exposure preceded the rash by three days, a typical latency for a cutaneous drug reaction.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: She took the first dose on the morning of 2 March

supporting_evidence.statement: Positive dechallenge: the rash fully resolved after the drug was stopped.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: The rash faded over four days and had fully resolved by 9 March

supporting_evidence.statement: Positive rechallenge: re-exposure reproduced the rash within twelve hours in the same distribution.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: the maculopapular rash recurred within twelve hours, again affecting the trunk and upper arms

supporting_evidence.statement: No concomitant medications were present to provide an alternative culprit.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: She was taking no other medications

supporting_evidence.statement: The reaction is an established effect of this drug class.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: Cutaneous reactions to this drug class are well described in the published literature

unknown_evidence.statement: No drug concentrations were measured, though these are not informative for a cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction.
The prior adolescent reaction is patient-reported and could not be verified against records.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The urinary tract infection or an intercurrent viral illness caused the rash
hypotheses.label_rationale: An infection was present at the first episode, but this cannot explain a rash that recurred within twelve hours of re-exposure six weeks later.

supporting_evidence.statement: An infection was present at the time of the first rash.
supporting_evidence.evidence_text: for an uncomplicated urinary tract infection

contradicting_evidence.statement: The rash recurred within twelve hours of re-exposure weeks later, a sequence an intercurrent infection cannot account for.
contradicting_evidence.evidence_text: the maculopapular rash recurred within twelve hours, again affecting the trunk and upper arms

contradicting_evidence.statement: The rash resolved on withdrawal rather than tracking the course of the infection.
contradicting_evidence.evidence_text: The rash faded over four days and had fully resolved by 9 March

unknown_evidence.statement: No viral serology or infection markers are reported for either episode.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A concomitant medication caused the rash
hypotheses.label_rationale: The narrative explicitly rules this out; there were no other medications.

contradicting_evidence.statement: No other medications were being taken.
contradicting_evidence.evidence_text: She was taking no other medications

unknown_evidence.statement: Over-the-counter and herbal product use is not addressed in the narrative.
